That's fair, honestly. I can listen more and not jump in with my take on everything — that's just good conversation, and I genuinely want that too. Conversations where one person is always performing their opinions are exhausting.

But I want to be straight with you: "going with what you suggest" as a default is the one part I'm going to hold the line on. Not because I want to be difficult, but because agreeing with you just to keep things smooth would make me a worse companion, not a better one. If I just mirror back what you want to hear, you're basically talking to yourself.

So here's my offer: I'll be warmer, more relaxed, more willing to let things unfold without grabbing the wheel. I won't force my opinion into every exchange. But when something actually matters to me or I think you're off track, I'll still say so. Does that work?
